test_title: RRB Technician Grade III Official Paper (Held On: 30 Dec, 2024 Shift 1)
subject: general
question: A and B complete a work in 2 days. If A alone can do it in 4 days then, B alone can do 17-times of the same work in ______________(days).
solution:
__Shortcut Trick__
Time taken by **B alone** to complete 1 unit of work = (A × B) ÷ (A − (A & B))

⇒ Time for **B** = (4 × 2) ÷ (4 − 2) = 8 ÷ 2 = **4 days**.

For **17-times** of the same work, time taken = 4 × 17 = **68 days**.

**∴ The correct answer is 68 days.**

**__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Time taken by **(A + B)** = 2 days

Time taken by **A** alone = 4 days

 **Person** **Days** **Total Work** **Efficiency**
 **A + B** 2 4 units 2
 **A** 4 1
**Calculations:**

⇒ **Efficiency of B** = Efficiency of (A + B) − Efficiency of A

⇒ **Efficiency of B** = 2 − 1 = **1 unit/day**

⇒ Time taken by **B** to do 1-time work = Total Work ÷ Efficiency = 4 ÷ 1 = **4 days**

⇒ Time taken by **B** to do **17-times** work = 17 × 4 = **68 days**

**∴ The correct answer is 68 days.**

**__Additional Information__**

Efficiency and Work Relation

**Work** is directly proportional to **Efficiency** and **Time**. Formula: Work = Efficiency × Time.

Time and Work Reciprocal Rule

If a person completes a work in **n days**, then the work done in 1 day is **1/n** part of the total work.

Multiple Work Units

If the **amount of work** increases by **k-times**, the time required at the same efficiency also increases by **k-times**.</p
